text:
maria: Quick proposal: introduce a "version-cascade" routing mode for v2 rollout. idea is to route by default to v2, but allow an ordered fallback chain (v2 -> v1-compat -> v1) for tenant requests when capacity or strict compatibility checks fail.
kevin: can we keep billing attribution tied to the original requested version? otherwise usage reports & invoices will be messy.
samir: strongly +1 for billing-attribution to the requested version. also need a clear event in telemetry that indicates actual served version vs requested version.
jess: UX question — in the console, how do we show routes that are served by a fallback? we shouldn't spam customers with alerts. maybe an aggregate badge + per-tenant drilldown? :thinking_face:
maria: yes — console should show a per-route "cascade index" metric: 0 = primary, 1 = first fallback, etc. default is aggregated but you can expand to see tenants and counts.
kevin: ops concern: we need guardrails so cascade doesn't mean silent quality regression. propose a hard cap on percent of traffic that can be auto-fallbacked per tenant and a tenant-level opt-out.
samir: technical: runtime already has fallback hooks but they lose original-request metadata when we short-circuit. we should add an "origin_version" field to the request context that persists through routing and to billing/telemetry. small change but touches many spans.
jess: console copy: "Requests may be routed to compatible variants when primary is unavailable. Billing and SLA reflect the original requested version." does that read ok?
kevin: also need alerting: if >1% of a route falls back to a lower-quality variant for more than 5m, page platform-oncall and notify product.
maria: noted. rollout plan thought: 1) instrumentation + origin_version tag; 2) console exposure + per-route cap UI; 3) soft rollout to 10% of tenants; 4) widen with QA.
ops-bot: deploy started: feature/route-cascade-instrumentation -> staging (ci/1234)
samir: implementation detail: telemetry events should include fields: ["requested_version", "served_version", "cascade_index", "fallback_reason"]. prefer snake_case to match existing pipelines.
maria: agree on fields. also add "cascade_telemetry_tag" for sampling to make it easy to query large datasets.
analytics-bot: note: existing billing pipeline expects a single "version" tag on usage events. will require a one-line mapping change to read requested_version first, fall back to served_version.
jess: UX for opt-out: per-tenant toggle labeled "Allow compatible fallbacks" with a tooltip explaining impact on latency and quality. default ON for early rollout?
kevin: default OFF for enterprise tenants; ON for PLG unless tenant has SLA flag. We need console policy that respects tenant tier.
maria: agreement: default ON for PLG, OFF for enterprise. add an override API for account teams.
samir: one more: KV cache keys differ across versions. if we fallback across model variants we must avoid cache poisoning. suggest namespacing cache by requested_version in cascade mode.
kevin: good catch. that implies minor perf hit when falling back but protects correctness.
maria: action items: @samir - design request context change + cache namespacing PR; @kevin - alerting & quota cap config UI; @jess - console copy and opt-out UX; I'll own rollout checklist and billing mapping.
samir: I'll target a staging PR by EOD tomorrow.
jess: drafted console copy here: 
```
Version cascade: routes may automatically fall back to compatible variants under capacity or compatibility constraints. Metrics show number of fallbacks and impact on quality. Toggle per-tenant in account settings.
```
kevin: looks good. add note about billing attribution.
maria: thanks team. we'll sync tomorrow 10am to lock SLA wording before any staging rollout. :thumbsup:
analytics-bot: event schema ticket created: ANLY-4829 (links to docs)
